questions.stem: In a hypothetical PIR, someone says: "This outage happened because Alice pushed wrong YAML. She should have tested it first." What is the BEST blameless response?

options.text: "You're right, Alice should have been more careful."
"This isn't Alice's fault, it's the system's fault."
"Let's discuss what process or validation would have caught this error before production."

questions.stem: The named VPC and attachment are absent when you collect evidence for a reported server-07 problem. Which statement is supported?

options.text: Their absence proves the webhook rejected them; check logs to find the exact error.
They were absent when checked; request submission history before naming a cause.
ArgoCD deleted them before collection; Git history will identify who caused it.
The switch is misconfigured; inspect ports before checking the request history.

questions.stem: Which action item is BEST (most SMART)?

options.text: Owner: Jordan. Due: 14 days. Remind operators to be more careful when writing reports.
Owner: Jordan. Due: 14 days. Improve the support checklist with useful details.
Owner: Jordan. Due: 14 days. Add YAML, submission result, test output and UTC time to intake; verify all four on the next practice report.
Owner: Jordan. Due: 14 days. Add a Gitea warning label and assume reports are complete.

questions.stem: Suppose five verified PIRs in one month identify the same configuration error. What is the BEST next step?

options.text: Accept that configuration issues are common
Compare the verified evidence, prioritize a systemic improvement, and check whether it reduces recurrence
Require operators to re-read the same documentation
Add more warning labels to Gitea
